explanation: Edison's phonograph of 1877 recorded on cylinders. Berliner's flat discs could be stamped out in large numbers from a single master, which made records cheap to mass-produce.

claims.text: Emile Berliner patented the gramophone, which played flat discs, in 1887.
Thomas Edison, Alexander Graham Bell and Guglielmo Marconi did not invent the gramophone.
Edison's phonograph of 1877 recorded sound on cylinders.
Gramophone discs could be mass-produced by pressing copies from a master.
